questions.question: Which Fundamental Right was added through the 86th Constitutional Amendment, 2002?

options.text: To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture
The parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education of his/her child/ward between the age of six and fourteen years.
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education of his/her child/ward between the age of six and fourteen years**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Right to Education** was made a **Fundamental Right** by the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**.
 
• **Part IV** of The Indian Constitution, **Article 45** and **Article 39 (f)** of DPSP, had the provision for equitable and accessible education.
 
• The Right to Education serves as a building block to ensure that every child has his/her right to get a quality education between the age of **six** and** fourteen** years.
 
• In **1993**, the Supreme Court’s judgment in the **Unnikrishnan JP vs State of Andhra Pradesh & Others** held that Education is a fundamental right.
 
• **Tapas Majumdar Committee (1999)** was set up, which comprehend the insertion of **Article 21A**.
 
• The 86th amendment provided legislation for the Right to Education Bill 2008 and finally the Right to Education Act 2009.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 21-A, Right to Education:** The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such manner as the State may, by law, determine.
 
• It had a clause for '**No Detention Policy'** which has been removed under **The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (Amendment) Act, 2019.**
 
• The act mandates 25% reservations for SC's and ST's , Socially Backward Class and Differently abled.
 
• It also focuses on making children free of fear, trauma, and anxiety through a system of child-friendly and child-centred learning.

questions.question: Quartz consists of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**silicon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Quartz** is a mineral composed of **silicon** and **oxygen**, with a chemical composition of **SiO₂**.
 
• **Metamorphic rocks** contain abundant quartz especially those products from **granites**, **sandstones**, or **shales**.
 
• **Sandstones are pure quartz.**
 
• **Rock crystal quartz** is found widely distributed in the **Alps**, **Brazil**, **Madagascar**, and **Japan**.
 
• Quartz exists in two forms, the normal temperature **α-quartz,** and the high-temperature **β-quartz**.
 
• The hardness of the quartz is measured by **Moh's Scale**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quartz** is one of the most useful natural materials. Its usefulness can be linked to its physical and chemical properties.
 
• It is chemically inert in contact with most substances. It has electrical properties and heat resistance.
 
• Its luster, color, and diaphaneity make it useful as a gemstone and also in the **making of glass**.
 
• Use of quartz as an Abrasive: Quartz sands and finely ground silica sand are used for sand blasting, scouring cleansers, and grit for sanding and sawing.
 
• Use of quartz in the Petrol industry.

questions.question: In how many classes are roads classified in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Six**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The roads are classified into **six** types: **National Highways**, **State Highways**, **District roads**, **Rural roads**, **Border Roads**, and **Expressways**.
 
• **National Highways** are the roads that connect one state with another and also connect important ports. These roads are constructed and laid by the **Central Public Works Department**(CPWD). They are designated with **NH**.
 
• **State Highways** are highways connecting major cities all over the state, it also connects other state highways of neighbouring states. It is designated by **SH**. State governments have the authority to build and maintain highways. Constructed and maintained by **Public Work Departments of state**.
 
• **District roads** are the roads where the districts are connected to each other. Other than a district, **Zila Parishads** also have the authority and responsibility to build roads.
 
• **Rural roads** are single-lane roads used to connect India's rural and remote areas. The roads are constructed and laid by **Panchayats** or by the project of **Pradhan Mantri Gramin Sadak Yojna**(PMGSY)
 
• **Border roads** are the roads constructed on the **North** and **North Eastern** borders of the country, constructed and maintained by the **Border Roads Organization **(BRO).
 
• **Expressways** are high-speed roads that are four or more lanes that have been designed for high-speed vehicular traffic, with all traffic flow regulated with toll roads. **National Expressways Authority of India** operates under the **Ministry of Road Transport and Highways**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The minister for the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways is **Nitin Gadkari**.
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Gramin Sadak Yojna(PMGSY)** was launched in December 2000, by the Indian Government to provide connectivity to isolated rural habitations.
 
• Border Road Organisation was set up in 1960 by the Government of India, it is regarded as the symbol of nation building, national integration and maintaining the security of the country.

questions.question: Which of the following was the first state to be annexed into the British empire under the Doctrine of Lapse introduced by Lord Dalhousie?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Satara__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first state to be annexed into the British empire under the Doctrine of Lapse was **Satara**, in the year **1848**.
 
• The Doctrine of Lapse was introduced by **Lord Dalhousie.**
 
• The **Doctrine of lapse** stated that: 
 
 
• The ruler of any princely state which governed directly or indirectly by the British does not have a legal male heir then his state will be annexed by the British.
 
• Adopted sons are not accepted as legal heirs of the policy.
 
 
 
• The scheme was the British annexation policy without a direct, natural, or adopted heir which was how the British acquire the many Indian States.
 
• The states that were annexed, followed by Satara were Jaitpur and Sambalpur(1849), Bhagat(1850), Udaipur(1852), Jhansi(1853), and Nagpur(1854).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lord Dalhousie was the Governor General of India from 1848-1856.
 
• He also introduced the Doctrine of Good of Governed under which Awadh and Punjab were annexed.
 
• Dalhousie established Public Works Department, the objective behind the formation of this department was the construction and maintenance of canals, roads, bridges, etc.
 
• Lord Dalhousie asserted that the western way of ruling was better than the eastern.

questions.question: Soft drinks consist of which of the following gases?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Carbon dioxide**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carbon dioxide** or **CO****₂** is present in soft drinks.
 
• The process of adding carbon dioxide to soft drinks is called **Carbonation**.
 
• **Carbonation** is the chemical reaction of carbon dioxide to give **carbonates**, **bicarbonates**, and **carbonic acid**.
 
• When the gaseous carbon dioxide comes in contact with water, it undergoes a chemical reaction to produce **aqueous carbonic acid.** 
 
• It is the carbonic acid that imparts the acidic flavor and a sweet sensation while drinking, without it, almost every soft drink tastes too bland.
 
• The **use** of carbon dioxide in soft drinks has various reasons such as being **highly soluble**, **preservative**, **cost-effective**, etc.
 
• The carbon dioxide that can be dissolved in water is described by **Henry's law**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sulphur dioxide** is the chemical compound with the formula SO₂. It is used as a food preservative and a bleaching agent.
 
• **Carbon monoxide** is colorless, highly poisonous, and tasteless, the formula is CO. It is used as a reducing agent in blast furnaces.
 
• **Nitrogen** is the chemical element with the formula N. The four major use of nitrogen is in Aircraft fuel systems, the light bulb industry, stainless steel manufacturing, and the preservation of food.

questions.question: The first modern Olympic Games under IOC was held in ______.

__
 
• The first modern Olympic Games(Summer Olympics) under International Olympic Games(IOC) were held in Athens, Greece in the year 1896.
 
• It was officially known as the **Games of the Olympiad**, and commonly known as '__**Athens 1896**'.
 
• Organized by the International Olympic Committee(IOC) which was created by **French Pierre de Coubertin**.
 
• There were 9 sporting events featured in the Summer Olympics in 1896.
 
• Fourteen nations and 241 athletes all males took part.

questions.question: The Kesariya Stupa is located in which Indian state?
questions.solution:

• **Kesariya stupa **is a Buddhist stupa in Kesariya, situated at a interval of **110 kilometres (68 mi) along with Patna, in the Champaran (east) district of Bihar city.**
 
• The Kesariya Stupa is known as** Devalaya,** the **house of Gods among the local community**.
 
• The stupa dates between 200 AD and 750 AD and may have been related to the **4th-century ruler, Raja Chakravarti. **
 
• **Kesariya Stupa is 104 feet high.**
 
• Kesariya came into the focus of attention after the **discovery of the biggest ever Buddhist Stupa.**

• **Buddhism** is be one of world's biggest religions and founded **2,500 years ago in India.**
 
• Buddhists trust that the human life is one of suffering, and that **meditation, spiritual and physical labor, and good manners are the ways to obtain knowledge, or nirvana.**
 
• Buddhism, as well known as** Buddha Dharma or Dharmavinaya**, is an Indian religion or philosophical ritual based on a series of original teachings** credited to Gautama Buddha.**

questions.question: Who among the following led the Salt Satyagraha march from Trichy to Vedaranyam in Tamil Nadu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chakravarti Rajgopalachari.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chakravarti Rajgopalachari** led the Salt Satyagraha march from **Trichy** to **Vedaranyam** in Tamil Nadu.
 
• C. Rajgopalachari began his march from Trichy on **April 13** and reached Vedaranyam on **April 28**.
 
• Inspired by **Mahatma Gandhi's Dandi March**, a group of 100 men extracted salt from seawater at Vedaranyam in April 1930, **to break the salt law imposed by the British**.
 
• The Salt Satyagraha was an act of the **Civil Disobedience Act** led by **Mahatma Gandhi** to protest British rule in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sundara Sastri Satyamurti**, commonly known as S. Satyamurti, was a well-known Indian freedom fighter and a reputed political leader.
 
• **Kumaraswami Kamaraj**, popularly known as Kamarajar was an Indian independence activist and politician, who served as the Chief Minister of Madras State from 13th April 1954 to 2nd October 1963.
 
• **Subramaniya Siva** was an Indian freedom fighter, writer, and pure Tamil movement activist during the Indian Independence Movement.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is NOT celebrated primarily in Arunachal Pradesh?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Losoong** festival is one of the prominent events in **Sikkim**, in North East India.
 
• The **Sikkimese New Year begins with Losoong**, which is celebrated with enthusiasm throughout the province.
 
• The event takes place at the end of the harvesting season, which gives joy and excitement to all of the farmers. 
 
• **Cham dances **performed by **Buddhist monks** are the main attraction of this festival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Sangken **festival is celebrated in Arunachal Pradesh and parts of Assam, India as a traditional new year's day from 14 to 16 April.

questions.question: Who among the following defeated the Lodhi sultan in the battle of Panipat in 1526 and founded the Mughal empire in medieval India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Babur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Babur** is the founder of the **Mughal Empire**.
 
• He fought the **first Battle of** **Panipat** in **1526 **against **Ibrahim Lodhi**, the last Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate. 
 
• The battle involved the earliest use of gun powders, firearms, and field artillery.
 
• His autobiography '**Tuzuk-i-Babri**' was written in the **Turkish **language.
 
• In 1527, his General Mir Baki built '**Babri Masjid**.'
 
• Babur died in **1530**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​Ibrahim Lodhi the last Sultan of Delhi Sultanate became Sultanate after the death of his father Sikandar Lodhi. Bahlul Lodhi was the chief of the Pashtun Lodhi Tribe.

 
 
• He was the founder of the Lodhi dynasty from the Delhi Sultanate.
 
 
 
• The Second Battle of Panipat in the year 1556, was fought between the forces of Samrat Hem Chandra Vikramaditya and the army of Akbar.
 
 
• The Akbar General's Khan Zaman I and Bairam Khan defeated the Hindu King.
 
 
 
• The Third Battle of Panipat in the year 1761 was fought between forces of the Maratha empire and the coalition of the King of Afghanistan, Ahmad Shah Durrani.
 
 
• Durrani's allies finally won and defeated Marathas.

questions.question: Jhika Dasain, a famous tribal dance of India, is predominantly performed by which of the following tribal groups?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Santhal__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jhika Dasain** is an Indian folk dance from **Jharkhand**.
 
• The Jhika Dasain is a form of worshiping dance practiced by the **Santal tribe**, to train young men of the community, the art of acquiring **spiritual powers** and dispelling the influence of **evil spirits**.
 
• The **training** lasts for several days, but the occasion when the spiritual powers are attained rejoices with a night-long 'Lagren' dance in which women also participate.
 
• The **musical instruments** played during the dance are Madar, a cylindrical drum, Nagade, a hemispherical single-face drum, and Jhal, the cymbals.
 
• This dance is performed a few days before **Dussehra**, it is prohibited to perform or sing any part of the song or dance after Dussehra.
 
• The dance is performed before every house and it is customary for the housewife to offer some grains to the dancers, which are finally sold for purchasing necessary materials for worshiping the **goddess** **Manasa** and the guru.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhils**, are considered one of the oldest tribes of India. Bhil is the largest tribal group in India, according to the 2011 Census living in **Chhatisgarh**,** Gujarat**, **Karnataka**, **Madhya Pradesh**, **Maharashtra**, **Andhra Pradesh**, and **Rajasthan**.
 
• **Kuki **people are ethnic group inhabiting the Nort-Eastern states of India such as **Manipur, Mizoram, and Assam.**
 
• **Gaddi **is an Indo-Aryan ethno-linguistic tribe living mainly in the Indian states of **Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir.**

• **Kuchipudi** is native to the **state of Andhra Pradesh** and varies from the other five classical styles by the inclusion of singing.

• Kuchipudi is a dance-drama presentation, with its roots in the old** Hindu Sanskrit text of Natya Shastra.**

• **Kathakali or 'story play**' arose in **Kerala in southern India** in the seventeenth century under the patronage of the** prince of Karnataka.**
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is a classical dance of **Tamil Nadu **in southern India.
 
• **Manipuri** is an old classical dance form that originated in the northeastern state of** Manipur in India.​**
